cases.notes: Approved browser authentication is represented without a cookie value.
Native password-provider REST uses its isolated cookie class.
Supported native OAuth or OIDC uses a source-issued bearer class without storing bearer material.
An invalid bearer class cannot silently fall back to a cookie class.
Missing authentication is a controlled denial.
An approved path does not authorize an unapproved method.
Source presence is not client authorization.
The ticket is modeled only as an ephemeral semantic class.
The bearer class is used only to mint a fresh ticket, never sent on upgrade.
A missing ticket cannot fall back to cookie, bearer, or legacy query state.
Reuse is denied and only a bounded semantic reason may remain in logs.
Expiry is a hard denial; the same ticket is never retried.
Local query-token mode is not a gated compatibility fallback.
PTY is web-only and its attach handle and bytes remain semantic and redacted.
Apple clients, including macOS, never invoke the full Terminal surface.
The PTY proof requires an attested POSIX or WSL host class.
The edge denial is not a Hermes upstream result.
Unsupported public host classes stop before the upstream process.
A Hermes 400 stays distinct from an edge denial.
A Hermes 4403 is not an edge 403.
The operation is approved without storing prompt text or a transcript.
Unknown operations do not trigger a guessed route or best-effort fallback.
Only the source-defined model key is in scope.
Malformed input uses only a non-sensitive marker and is capped before log retention.
An additive noninteractive event may be ignored.
Unknown interactive events never become approval or clarification UI.
Logs retain no ticket, attach handle, input, output, or transcript bytes.
Provider discovery is semantic and never stores provider credentials.
Password-provider login is represented without password text or cookie values.
The protected cookie mints a fresh gated ticket without retaining its value.
The reviewed native bearer route mints a fresh gated ticket without storing bearer material.
Native authorization is reviewed only when the deployment advertises the route.
Native token exchange is represented as a reviewed route result without token material.
Native refresh is represented as a reviewed route result without refresh material.
A fresh ticket does not compensate for missing Upgrade and Connection headers.
Malformed ticket syntax is denied separately from missing, expired, reused, or invalid tickets.
PTY requires both HTTP upgrade headers in addition to a fresh ticket.
Malformed PTY ticket syntax is denied without retaining the ticket or attach handle.
WSL is a separately observed supported web PTY host class.
iOS does not request the web-only PTY route.
iPadOS does not request the web-only PTY route.
macOS does not request the web-only PTY route.
An unknown reviewed-path boundary returns an edge 404 without calling Hermes upstream.
Duplicate JSON keys are rejected before a later value can hide a mutation.
A JSON array or scalar top level is rejected without retaining its contents.
Invalid UTF-8 is rejected with a semantic marker and no source bytes.
Malformed JSON syntax maps to JSON-RPC parse error -32700.
Oversized valid JSON integers are rejected before numeric conversion.
Deep JSON nesting is rejected before a path or payload is retained.
Secret-shaped and huge object keys are rejected without echoing the key.
Reconnect uses a fresh ticket and does not replay a prompt.
Chat close is a detach observation, not an immediate server kill.
Session resume restores the server-owned identity before any prompt retry.
Transport loss never becomes an automatic duplicate prompt submission.
Synthetic attestation match is recorded but cannot enable compatibility.
A source mismatch blocks the gate and remains non-live.
Caddy approval records only reviewed mapped headers.
Caddy edge denial is kept separate from upstream results.
Traefik approval records the same semantic mapped headers.
Traefik edge denial is kept separate from upstream results.
Web consumes the shared semantic fixture and owns the Terminal route.
iOS consumes the shared semantic fixture and never requests PTY.
iPadOS consumes the shared semantic fixture and never requests PTY.
macOS consumes the shared semantic fixture and never requests PTY.

accessibility.reason: This issue creates a non-UI protocol fixture and standard-library validator; it adds no controls, focus order, semantic names, screen-reader or VoiceOver surface, Switch Control behavior, Dynamic Type or browser zoom layout, contrast, motion, transparency, or touch target.
accessibility.preservation: The fixture does not remove downstream web or Apple accessibility obligations; later clients must preserve those checks while showing the blocked compatibility state safely.
